docs.purpose: The form on which an operator assigns a specific advertiser to a specific advertising slot in the product — which sponsor appears where, and for how long. The list of valid slots is a closed, declared set rather than free text, so a placement cannot be pointed at a slot that does not exist. Today the component that would display a sponsor renders nothing at all, so there is no way to sell or schedule a placement.

rls_class.why: DECISION NEEDED (Spec 114): `offers` is Class D (advertiser select/update own), but `placements` is declared in Spec 126 §6.3 row 5 as "anon / user / advertiser select; admin all" — a PUBLICLY READABLE table. Spec 114 §2's taxonomy is closed and definitional (A = one of the 10 named auth.uid()-owned tables, B = RLS-on-with-ZERO-policies default-deny, C = profiles, D = owner-scoped by a non-user key) and has no class for a table anon may read. Answering "B" would be false (B denies anon outright, Spec 114 §4); answering "D" would be false (placements has no owner column). Spec 114 must take the decision before the migration is authored.

checks.why: R-12 / Spec 128 §3 rule B6: every admin mutation writes exactly one admin_audit_log row and an audit failure fails the request. It is blocking because 9 of the 15 mutating admin routes measured today write no row at all, and the pre-batch rule says an unaudited mutation blocks conversion of the surface that calls it.

R-17/R-34: a placement whose disclosure_required is false cannot be saved for a surface that renders to a user. The legal basis is Competition Act s.74.01 and the Competition Bureau native-advertising guidance, plus the FTC Native Advertising Guide (2015) / 16 CFR Part 255 — which is why severity FAIL and blocking true are SEPARATE fields, and blocking forces when "pre".
Rule 14: neither placements nor offers exists, so every declared column, CHECK vocabulary, FK and policy is asserted against the live catalog both directions before the form writes.
The FORM profile requires an error state; a save that silently fails would bill an advertiser for a placement that never rendered.
The form's field set must set-equal its contract's projection — the measured "one contract declared at four sites, locked at one" defect Spec 128 rule 4 names.
R-18: the same offers rows are read by the advertiser principal through Class D, so a mutation contract drifting off admin would hand an advertiser its own scheduling form.
Every control on a form that sets a legal disclosure flag carries an accessible label.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM offers WHERE flight_end IS NOT NULL AND flight_start IS NOT NULL AND flight_end < flight_start
invariants.why: A flight that ends before it starts renders zero impressions while reading as scheduled — an advertiser paying for nothing, invisible in every count.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM offers o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM placements p WHERE p.placement_key = o.placement_key)
invariants.why: The closed placement vocabulary is the point: an offer pointed at a slot that does not exist can never render, and the FK plus this assertion are what make "never a literal" true.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT o.placement_key, count(*) AS n FROM offers o WHERE o.active GROUP BY 1) x JOIN placements p USING (placement_key) WHERE x.n > p.max_slots
invariants.why: max_slots is the declared cap the SLOT archetype renders against; oversubscription is a commercial state an operator may create deliberately, so it warns rather than fails — but it is never silent.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT disclosure_required), count(*) FROM placements
plausibility.why: Any placement rendering to a user without disclosure_required is a legal exposure, not a preference; the expected count is zero and a non-zero one is a defect rather than a signal.

limitations.what: The admin_audit_log row this surface writes cannot be named in emits.ledger_events[].
limitations.measured: surface.schema.json's emits.ledger_events[] is closed to property_view · pdf_send · offer_impression · offer_click · export · parcel_id_translated — all usage_events events. admin_audit_log is a second append-only ledger (Spec 126 §2.2.1 P10 names all three by name) with no token, so emits.answer is "ledger" and the audit row is carried in breadcrumbs[] plus a ledger_row_present check.

limitations.what: guards.rls_class is UNRESEARCHED because Spec 114's closed taxonomy cannot express `placements`.
limitations.measured: Spec 126 §6.3 row 5 declares anon/user/advertiser select on placements; Spec 114 §4 says Class B denies anon outright and §2 says everything not A/C/D is B. There is no class for a publicly-readable table, so the migration cannot be authored until Spec 114 rules.

notes: Report §1.1 row 14. Measured defect it makes visible: SponsorSlot returns null on both branches, i.e. the slot is dead in the product. TREE CORRECTION: the report writes this file as `SponsorSlot.tsx (21L)` with no path; the file actually lives at mobile/src/components/parcel/SponsorSlot.tsx (there is no src/components/SponsorSlot.tsx), so this is a MOBILE component even though the managing surface is web. VERIFIED: no CREATE TABLE for placements in migrations/. DESIGNED, NOT MEASURED. guards.rls_class is deliberately UNRESEARCHED: Spec 126 §6.3 row 5 gives placements an anon-readable posture that Spec 114 §2's closed four-class taxonomy has no value for, and inventing a fifth class per-row is exactly the escalation the research brief §4 rule 1 forbids. The disclosure check is FAIL + blocking as SEPARATE fields per R-17/R-34 — the schema models them separately because they are orthogonal, and blocking true forces when "pre".
